svg.title: CoreLR geometry
svg.desc: Dimensions, coordinate frames, calibration and cable lengths of the CoreLR wall plotter, D = 1000 mm, Lref = 700 mm
svg.text: CoreLR geometry: what to measure, what to enter, what the firmware assumes

Example machine D = 1000 mm, Lref = 700 mm: NOT the maintainer's machine (the firmware's factory values are 0, so both must be entered). Every figure on this page is computed from the formulas and checked
against the firmware's own code by tools/generators/gen_geometry_svg.py --verify.
A. The machine seen from the front, to scale (0.78 px per mm); the casings are schematic
line of the two exit holes
D = distance between the two cable exit holes = 1000 mm (LCD: "Motor dist (mm)")
tape measure, exit hole to pen, on both cables
depth of O below the exit holes
INTERNAL frame (violet), used only by the kinematics:
origin at the exit hole of motor L, X to the right, Y DOWN.
O is at (D/2, H) = (500, 489.898). Never shown.
DRAWING frame (green): GCode, LCD, status report.
B. The test square 200 x 200 mm, zoomed (1.75 px per mm)
L and R: cable lengths in mm at each point, exit hole to pen (formulas in C). Top
row: both cables shorter than Lref; bottom row: both longer.
C. Formulas (drawing frame, mm; the firmware computes in whole micrometres)
D (between the two cable exit holes, the pivots) and Lref (cable length at the
H = sqrt(Lref^2 - (D/2)^2) = 489.898 mm. The origin is H BELOW the line of the exit
X = x + D/2, Y = H - y (so O is (D/2, H)).
2037.9 steps per turn, spool 35 mm: 109.956 mm per turn = 54 um per step.
Intended: MORE steps = LONGER cable, on both motors. Software direction flags in
HwConfig.h: L reversed = 1, R reversed = 0 (flipped 2026-10-10 after the bench).
A GCode target of 2097.152 mm or more in X or Y is refused (error:33).
At O: L = R = Lref. Moving up (+y) shortens both cables, down lengthens both; +x lengthens L and shortens
The LCD's L,R line shows these two lengths in mm; its X,Y line shows x and y.
D. Calibration on the LCD: main menu > Calibrate machine
1. Measure D with a tape, between the two cable exit holes. Enter it: "Motor dist (mm)".
2. Choose Lref > D/2 (for instance 700 mm). Enter it: "Ref length (mm)". The firmware then knows H.
3. Adjustment jog: X selects [L] or [R], Y winds or unwinds that cable. Bring the pen to the point
where BOTH cables measure Lref (tape, exit hole to pen): on the vertical through the middle, H
under the line of the exit holes.
4. SW = confirm. The firmware declares the pen to be at (0, 0) with L = R = Lref. It cannot check it.
Then "Calibrate pen" sets the two servo angles (factory 60 and 95). The position survives power cuts;
moving the motors by hand while off requires a new calibration.
- Each motor is a POINT: the cable leaves it through a FIXED hole in the casing of the winder (confirmed
by the maintainer, 2026-10-10), so the exit hole is the pivot and does not move with the cable's
direction. L and R are the straight lengths from that hole to the pen.
- The pen is the point where both cables meet (no offset between the cable attachment and the pen tip).
- The steps wind a constant 54 um of cable per step (the layers building up on the spool are ignored).
- O is where you calibrate, not necessarily the centre of the paper. Nothing in the firmware measures the
wall, the cables or the pen: D, Lref and step 3 are the maintainer's measurements.
